claim.exact_statement: Let h be the Boolean sign gate on six uniform physical inputs negative at binary indices {0,1,2,4,8,16,32,6,17,40}, with zero bits encoding +1. Define g0=h, g1=h(g0^6), g2=h((-g1)^6), and g3=h(g2^6), each substitution on six identical disjoint copies. Then g3 is an actual 1296-bit transitive Boolean function with 0<p_min(g3)<1/16 and E(g3)>669/200, where E is the minimum relevant-coordinate conditional Fourier erasure entropy divided by its physical influence, in bits. Both 7776-bit children h(g3^6) and h((-g3)^6) have E<669/200, and both corresponding signed recentered reserves are strictly negative at every physical coordinate. Hence common-sign six-bit admission does not preserve the fixed threshold 669/200 even on high-E actual cores. Moreover, for any actual core with minority probability 0<s<=1/16, either common output orientation in this substitution gives 0<s_next<=12s^2<=(3/4)s, so this rare bias sector is absorbing under every future sign sequence.

claim.exact_statement: Let h:{-1,1}^6->{-1,1} be negative at binary indices {0,1,2,4,8,16,32,6,17,40}, with zero encoding sign +1, and let J(x)=-h(x xor1). For every nonconstant actual uniform-cube Boolean seed g, consider any finite strategy consisting of common-policy h substitutions and optional complete J rare-escape episodes, always using six identical cores with disjoint physical supports. A common step chooses minority-negative inputs when minority s<=7/32 and complements all six inputs otherwise; output signs may be reoriented to minority. A J episode is allowed only at 0<s<=1/16 and repeatedly substitutes J on minority-oriented copies until the first minority bias above1/16; a final output may stop inside an episode. Then every resulting actual finite Boolean F satisfies H(F)/I(F)<=H(g)/I(g)+(1731/44)*Var(g)/I(g)<H(g)/I(g)+40, in entropy bits. The proof uses mu=Var/I, which contracts by at least2/3 at each common h step and never increases at J steps; a common step costs at most8mu in normalized entropy and an entire escape episode costs at most(225/44)mu_start. Thus arbitrarily many eligible escape/return cycles from a fixed finite seed cannot yield an unbounded-H/I disproof.

(a) ghat_N(S) = fhat(S)*1{S subset [n]} - 2p f(x0) chi_S(x0) for every S subset [N]; for every A subset [N] the coefficient of g_N*chi_A at [N] is nonzero, so d_{g_N chi_A}(S) = N for every S and every anchor A, and U(g_N) = N Var(g_N) - I(g_N). (b) |I_i(g_N) - I_i(f)| <= 2p for every i, so |I(g_N) - I(f)| <= 2Np. (c) the spectral laws satisfy ||p(g_N) - p(f)||_1 <= 4p(2^(n/2) + 1), and |H(g_N) - H(f)| <= eps N + h2(eps) with eps = 2p(2^(n/2) + 1). (d) for nonconstant f, H(g_N) -> H(f), I(g_N) -> I(f) and U(g_N)/I(g_N) -> infinity. (e) if psi(s,N) >= 0 with max_s psi(s,N) = o(2^N) and Psi(g) = sum over nonempty S with ghat(S) != 0 of ghat(S)^2 psi(|S|, d_g(S)), then Psi(g_N) - sum_{S nonempty} fhat(S)^2 psi(|S|, N) -> 0; hence an inequality H <= alpha I + beta Var + Psi valid for all Boolean functions implies H(f) <= alpha I(f) + beta Var(f) + liminf_N sum_{S nonempty} fhat(S)^2 psi(|S|, N) for all Boolean f. (f) FEI with constant C on the class {g_N} implies FEI with constant C for all Boolean functions.
